Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `PR #80` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

**Anything flagged here goes in your next status update to Marcel, even when it's correctly out
of scope for the PR itself.** "Not my concern for this review" and "not worth telling him" are
different judgements — a discovery can be exactly right to leave alone in the diff and still be
something he needs to know exists. Deciding not to act on it is not the same as deciding not to
mention it.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip. **Before concluding a state is simply absent from a
  component, check whether an adjacent or parent element carries that same signal instead** (the
  button not the swatch, the row not the cell) — a concern can be fully handled by the design and
  still look like a gap if you only look at the one element it doesn't live on.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

---

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
discipline before it is presented as fact — a finding is not exempt from scrutiny just because no
agent produced it. Route it through the same questions: what is the search scope, does one
uncorroborated source actually settle this, and has a stated number been measured or only assumed.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open. No opening praise or thanks before the substance — a
review comment states findings, it does not warm up first. Watch for jargon-stacking too: a
sentence naming three technical concepts back to back reads like documentation, not like one
person explaining something to another — split it or say it plainer instead.

**Never reveal that a parallel or competing implementation of the same ticket exists**, even in
passing ("the other version of this feature," "the other build") — a review comment is visible to
the whole team, and disclosing a second, independent attempt at the same story is not this
reviewer's call to make. When a content rule like this applies, sweep every drafted comment for
it before presenting the batch, not just the one currently under discussion — a rule caught on
one comment and missed on a near-identical one is a leak, not a style nit.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

diff --git a/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml b/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
index 94950a2..3f65f1c 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
@@ -33,8 +33,23 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install Playwright browsers
         run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium
 
+      # Provisional: no *.p0.spec files exist anywhere in the repo yet (still early
+      # development — see .docs/memory/projectState.md). --pass-with-no-tests keeps the
+      # gate from permanently blocking every release branch on that basis alone, while a
+      # real P0 spec that actually fails still fails the job normally — this only changes
+      # the zero-tests case. The warning below keeps a "pass" from reading as real coverage —
+      # scoped to match the `p0` Playwright project's own testDir/testMatch exactly
+      # (playwright.config's testDir: './e2e', p0 project's testMatch: '**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}'),
+      # not just e2e/tests/zimm — a spec anywhere else under e2e/ that the project would
+      # actually pick up must not trip a false "no coverage" warning.
+      - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
+        run: |
+          if ! find e2e -name '*.p0.spec.js' -o -name '*.p0.spec.ts' | grep -q .; then
+            echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."
+          fi
+
       - name: Run P0 suite
-        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
+        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github --pass-with-no-tests
         env:
           RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}
 
@@ -84,8 +99,31 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install dependencies
         run: npm install --include=dev
 
+      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.
+      # Step-scoped (not job-level) so npm install's lifecycle scripts — which inherit
+      # job-level env but not this step's — never see the credential.
       - name: Run Lighthouse CI
         run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun
+        env:
+          LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL }}
+
+      # Lighthouse records collect.settings.extraHeaders verbatim in each report's
+      # configSettings — confirmed against a real run — so the access-control secret would
+      # otherwise sit in plain text inside the artifact this job uploads next. Redact before
+      # upload rather than trust nothing downstream ever inspects that field. Fail closed on a
+      # jq error: the next step still runs on `if: always()`, so a report left unredacted by a
+      # failed jq pass must not survive to be uploaded — delete it instead of uploading it as-is.
+      - name: Redact secrets from Lighthouse reports before upload
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          shopt -s nullglob
+          for f in .lighthouseci/lhr-*.json; do
+            if ! jq '.configSettings.extraHeaders |= (if . then with_entries(.value = "[REDACTED]") else . end)' "$f" > "$f.tmp"; then
+              rm -f "$f" "$f.tmp"
+              continue
+            fi
+            mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
+          done
 
       - name: Upload Lighthouse results
         if: always()

     collect: {

{"baseRefName":"release/v0.1.0","body":"## Summary\n- `playwright-p0` hard-failed with \"No tests found\" — no `*.p0.spec` files exist anywhere in the repo yet (confirmed against `develop` too, not specific to this branch). Adds `--pass-with-no-tests` plus a visible `::warning::` annotation so a zero-spec pass never reads as real coverage; a genuine P0 failure once specs exist still fails the gate normally.\n- `lighthouse-ci` failed with `CHROME_INTERSTITIAL_ERROR` — `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` was never configured as a repo secret, so Lighthouse silently fell back to an unserved `localhost:3000`. Now points at the real SIT MRT URL and forwards the `x-sfdc-access-control` header its now-secured URL requires (also via a new `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` secret).\n- SIT was also bootstrapped with a real deployed build (`npm run push:sit` from `develop`) to break the deploy-then-gate/gate-then-deploy circularity — confirmed serving live content at the SIT MRT URL.\n\nPart of resuming tag-based release tagging (Sprint 1 → `v0.1.0`) — see `.claude/rules/tagging.md`.\n\n## Test plan\n- [ ] Confirm this PR's own SIT Gate run goes green (playwright-p0 soft-pass + warning annotation, lighthouse-ci against live SIT)\n- [ ] Merge to `release/v0.1.0`, then cut the final `v0.1.0` tag on the resulting tip","files":[{"path":".github/workflows/digital-sit.yml","additions":14,"deletions":1,"changeType":"MODIFIED"},{"path":"lighthouserc.js","additions":8,"deletions":0,"changeType":"MODIFIED"}],"headRefName":"fix/release-v0.1.0-sit-gate-recovery","mergedAt":null,"number":75,"state":"OPEN","title":"fix(ci): unblock SIT Gate for release/v0.1.0","url":"https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/75"}

diff --git a/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml b/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
index 495ab37..3f65f1c 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml
@@ -37,10 +37,14 @@ jobs:
       # development — see .docs/memory/projectState.md). --pass-with-no-tests keeps the
       # gate from permanently blocking every release branch on that basis alone, while a
       # real P0 spec that actually fails still fails the job normally — this only changes
-      # the zero-tests case. The warning below keeps a "pass" from reading as real coverage.
+      # the zero-tests case. The warning below keeps a "pass" from reading as real coverage —
+      # scoped to match the `p0` Playwright project's own testDir/testMatch exactly
+      # (playwright.config's testDir: './e2e', p0 project's testMatch: '**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}'),
+      # not just e2e/tests/zimm — a spec anywhere else under e2e/ that the project would
+      # actually pick up must not trip a false "no coverage" warning.
       - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
         run: |
-          if ! find e2e/tests/zimm -name '*.p0.spec.*' | grep -q .; then
+          if ! find e2e -name '*.p0.spec.js' -o -name '*.p0.spec.ts' | grep -q .; then
             echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."
           fi
 
@@ -84,8 +88,6 @@ jobs:
       LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
       LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
       LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
-      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.
-      LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
@@ -97,8 +99,31 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install dependencies
         run: npm install --include=dev
 
+      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.
+      # Step-scoped (not job-level) so npm install's lifecycle scripts — which inherit
+      # job-level env but not this step's — never see the credential.
       - name: Run Lighthouse CI
         run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun
+        env:
+          LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL }}
+
+      # Lighthouse records collect.settings.extraHeaders verbatim in each report's
+      # configSettings — confirmed against a real run — so the access-control secret would
+      # otherwise sit in plain text inside the artifact this job uploads next. Redact before
+      # upload rather than trust nothing downstream ever inspects that field. Fail closed on a
+      # jq error: the next step still runs on `if: always()`, so a report left unredacted by a
+      # failed jq pass must not survive to be uploaded — delete it instead of uploading it as-is.
+      - name: Redact secrets from Lighthouse reports before upload
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          shopt -s nullglob
+          for f in .lighthouseci/lhr-*.json; do
+            if ! jq '.configSettings.extraHeaders |= (if . then with_entries(.value = "[REDACTED]") else . end)' "$f" > "$f.tmp"; then
+              rm -f "$f" "$f.tmp"
+              continue
+            fi
+            mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
+          done
 
       - name: Upload Lighthouse results
         if: always()

1	name: SIT Gate
2	
3	on:
4	  push:
5	    branches:
6	      - 'release/**'
7	  pull_request:
8	    branches:
9	      - 'release/**'
10	
11	permissions:
12	  contents: read
13	  issues: write
14	  pages: write
15	  id-token: write
16	
17	jobs:
18	  playwright-p0:
19	    name: Playwright P0 journeys
20	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
21	    continue-on-error: false
22	    steps:
23	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
24	
25	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
26	        with:
27	          node-version: '24'
28	          cache: 'npm'
29	
30	      - name: Install dependencies
31	        run: npm install --include=dev
32	
33	      - name: Install Playwright browsers
34	        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium
35	
36	      - name: Run P0 suite
37	        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
38	        env:
39	          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}
40	
41	      - name: Upload Playwright report
42	        if: always()
43	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
44	        with:
45	          name: playwright-report
46	          path: playwright-report/
47	          retention-days: 30
48	
49	      - name: Upload Pages artifact
50	        if: always()
51	        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
52	        with:
53	          path: playwright-report/
54	
55	  deploy-playwright-report:
56	    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
57	    needs: playwright-p0
58	    if: always()
59	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
60	    environment:
61	      name: github-pages
62	      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
63	    steps:
64	      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
65	        id: deployment
66	        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
67	
68	  lighthouse-ci:
69	    name: Lighthouse CI
70	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
71	    continue-on-error: false
72	    env:
73	      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
74	      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
75	      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
76	    steps:
77	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
78	
79	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
80	        with:
81	          node-version: '24'
82	          cache: 'npm'
83	
84	      - name: Install dependencies
85	        run: npm install --include=dev
86	
87	      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
88	        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun
89	
90	      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
91	        if: always()
92	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
93	        with:
94	          name: lighthouse-results
95	          path: .lighthouseci/
96	          retention-days: 30
97	
98	  contract-tests:
99	    name: MuleSoft contract tests
100	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
101	    continue-on-error: false
102	    steps:
103	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
104	
105	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
106	        with:
107	          node-version: '24'
108	          cache: 'npm'
109	
110	      - name: Install dependencies
111	        run: npm install --include=dev
112	
113	      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
114	      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
115	      - name: Run contract tests
116	        run: npm run test:contracts
117	
118	  bundle-size:
119	    name: Bundle size check
120	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
121	    continue-on-error: false
122	    steps:
123	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
124	
125	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
126	        with:
127	          node-version: '24'
128	          cache: 'npm'
129	
130	      - name: Install dependencies
131	        run: npm install --include=dev
132	
133	      - name: Build and check bundle size
134	        run: npm run test:max-file-size
135	
136	  sit-gate:
137	    name: SIT Gate
138	    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
139	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
140	    if: always()
141	    steps:
142	      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
143	        run: |
144	          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
145	             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \

file.content:
name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"

on:

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # actually pick up must not trip a false "no coverage" warning.
      - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
        run: |
          if ! find e2e -name '*.p0.spec.js' -o -name '*.p0.spec.ts' | grep -q .; then
            echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."
          fi

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github --pass-with-no-tests
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.

              continue
            fi
            mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
          done

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"

# Project State

See In Progress). Previous: 2026-08-18 (zimmTokens.ts made fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files instead of hand-retyped literals; `zimmButton.css.ts` established as the single source of truth for button styling, `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*` class system removed; `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem for WCAG 1.4.4; `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` token convention; new `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the resulting styling-source hierarchy. See What's Complete). Previous: 2026-07-16 (PR #30 and PR #35 merged — e2e-localhost fixed and re-enabled, root cause was a swallowed click failure in `BasePage.js`'s consent handling; `deploy-test.yml` added for the previously undeployable `test` tier; README command reference added; Stage/UAT promotion order reconciled across docs; a tag-based environment-promotion proposal is drafted on Confluence, not yet implemented — see What's Pending). Previous sweep 2026-06-25 against updated Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx via /update-prds-from-xlsx — CFD-067 Company Name + VAT/Tax ID optional fields confirmed for EU/UK checkout; PRC-03 future-dated markdown with timezone mapping confirmed; PRC-07 tax class via AP21 taxonomy ID + Avalara/Global-e coverage confirmed; PRC-13 catalogue markdowns + promotions in order payload confirmed; PRC-46 coupon handling at Global-e challenged and kept Open; HPC-018 header icon set resolved — Search/Account/Bag only, Locate Boutique/Contact Us/Newsletter confirmed not in header; SPR-03 editorial paragraph confirmed not collapsible, read-more action only); trimmed stale entries.*

## Phase

Workshop sign-off tracker: All workshops signed off (2026-04-30 through 2026-06-24). Row-level opens tracked under Unresolved Dependencies below.

*For system roles and integration details, see [architecture.md](architecture.md). Open items that block implementation are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" below.*

## Integrations

## What's Complete

Delivered as a foundation for the manual UI build (branch `feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev`); F2R component work continues separately on `feature/f2r-component-registry` and `feature/f2r-implementation-workflow`. Open with the UI designer: primary-action hover contrast (2.96:1), inverse focus ring, and button-height / nav letter-spacing deviations from the Handover.
- **Token architecture hardened** (2026-08-18): `zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry) is now fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files via imports instead of hand-duplicated literals, closing the drift risk the original port above carried. `typography.ts` gained a proper `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights` scale layer. `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem (WCAG 1.4.4); within those two files, px is kept only for hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets — now named tokens in `spacing.ts`'s `focusRingOffsets`). `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding constants are a separate, already-flagged px exception (not hairline geometry) — see below. `zimmButton.css.ts` is now the single source of truth for button styling — `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*`/`.zimm-text-btn-*` classes (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states) were removed entirely; any button must use Chakra's `<Button>`, never a class. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` convention (no direct `foundation/` imports, no Chakra semantic colour-token names). New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the styling-source hierarchy, unit rules, the alias-is-a-reference-not-a-copy principle, and a real gotcha: importing an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path resolves correctly in the real app but silently renders the unstyled base version in Storybook/Vitest (the `ccExtensibility` resolver is webpack-only, neither tool loads it). Still open, flagged inline rather than silently resolved: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px prototype values) disagree with the Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all — both pending UI-designer sign-off.
- **Header override** (`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`): two-row layout, brand logo via `BrandLogo` component (overrides base SVG at `overrides/app/assets/svg/brand-logo.svg`), uppercase nav with `::after` hover animation, Account/Saved/Bag text buttons with matching animation, chevrons hidden. Still being refined visually against Figma.
- Path aliases (`~` → root, `app` → `overrides/app`) wired up across Babel, tsconfig, Storybook, and Jest
- **Per-tier environment switching** (`npm run env` → `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`) — manages `.env.shared` / `.env.<tier>` across dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod via `init` (scaffold + pull + Contentful auto-fetch), `validate [--live]` (structural checks plus live Contentful Delivery API + SFCC SLAS guest-token calls), and `push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only). Shared/tier values (excluding personal credentials) can be centrally published through this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per tier) — write gated to repo Admin. Landed 2026-07-13.

## In Progress

## What's Pending

  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.

Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.

    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.

All ground truth is gathered and every claim traced to source. Here's the full picture.

## PR #80 — `fix(ci): unblock SIT Gate for every release branch`

**fix/sit-gate-bootstrap → develop** · 2 files, +47/−1 · 3 real commits behind 6 rounds of CodeRabbit iteration, all today · author TimLavelleACC

### Gate table

| Gate | Base (`develop`) | Head (PR #80) | Executed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actionlint` on `digital-sit.yml` | 0 issues | 0 issues | Yes, both — real run |
| `shellcheck` (actionlint's embedded check on the new `run:` blocks) | n/a | 0 issues | Yes — the `find` and `jq` logic passes static shell analysis |
| `tsc --noEmit` / `npm run test` / `npm run lint` / `audit:tokens` | — | — | **Not run** — verified by path, not assumed: zero `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.test.ts` files touched, and `lint`'s actual invocation is scoped to `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` (confirmed from its own command line), `audit:tokens` scoped to `overrides/app/components`+`theme/components`. None of the four gates can see this diff. |
| Live CI on PR #80 itself | — | Branch/Squad checks + Unit tests pass; Storybook/E2E/BrowserStack skipped (unrelated files) | **`digital-sit.yml` itself never runs** — it triggers only on push/PR to `release/**`. A `develop`-targeted PR gets zero live signal on the actual logic being changed. |

### Findings

**1. [CONFIRMED, out-of-scope but urgent] PR #75 — still open, targets the live `release/v0.1.0` (171 commits ahead of `main`) — never received PR #80's three hardening commits.**
Branch `fix/release-v0.1.0-sit-gate-recovery`, unchanged since `8bc04d3`. I diffed the two branches directly: PR #75 still has the narrower `find e2e/tests/zimm` spec-scan, `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` at job-level (exposed to `npm install`'s lifecycle scripts — exactly what PR #80 fixed), and no redaction step before the Lighthouse artifact upload — meaning if PR #75 merges as-is, the access-control secret ships to a GitHub Actions artifact in plaintext. Same author on both PRs, so this is a backport he can do himself, not a communication gap. Also worth knowing: there's a separate Claude Code session on this machine titled **"ZIMM - PR #75 Review"** (idle) that may already be looking at this — worth checking before duplicating effort.

**2. [CONFIRMED, out-of-scope, pre-existing] `digital-sit.yml`'s `lighthouse-ci` job still job-scopes `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`/`LHCI_TOKEN`/`LHCI_TARGET_URL`** (lines 72-75), exposing them to the same `npm install` step PR #80 just excluded `LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` from — same pattern, left half-fixed. This predates PR #80 (present in the `develop` baseline already), so it's inherited debt, not a new violation. Practical risk today is low: `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`/`LHCI_TOKEN` aren't configured as real secrets at all (absent from `gh secret list` — they resolve to empty strings), and `LHCI_TARGET_URL` is a URL, not a bypass credential.

**3. [Verified, non-issue] The cross-origin secret leak CodeRabbit flagged (`lighthouserc.js:10-12`) is real — confirmed independently via Lighthouse's own installed source (`Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders` is session-wide, not origin-scoped, so `x-sfdc-access-control` goes to every third-party request the audited page makes, not just SIT).** This is the one place I'd have raised a blocker — except the author already found it, tried and disproved three separate fixes with live-SIT evidence (request interception breaks Lighthouse's own CDP session; the SIT gateway doesn't accept cookies; GitHub's runner IP pool is 29x over the gateway's allowlist cap), and filed **SFCC-864** to track it. I had a sub-agent independently verify that ticket exists and matches the claim in detail — it does. Nothing to add here.

### Scope verdict: **IN SCOPE**

Independently confirmed (I checked myself, and had zm-orchestrator check separately): the diff matches the PR body exactly, nothing unmentioned, nothing missing, and the "unchanged since June/July" claim about both files checks out against `git log`.

### What nobody verified

- Zero live-CI signal exists for this diff — `digital-sit.yml` can't trigger on a `develop`-targeted PR. Everything above rests on static analysis (`actionlint`/`shellcheck`) and manual source-tracing (Lighthouse's CDP behavior, `@lhci/utils`' `lhr-*.json` naming, Playwright's `p0` project scope), not an actual execution.
- I can't verify `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` resolves to a real, reachable SIT URL — secret values aren't visible to me.
- No Jira ticket covers the core fix itself (only the SFCC-864 follow-up) — consistent with this being infra/tooling work under the tagging.md initiative rather than a story, but flagging since I couldn't confirm that against a ticket.

Nothing here rises to an in-scope defect in PR #80 itself, so there's no draft PR comment queued unless you want the item 2 nudge posted.

content.text:
Here's the plain version.

**The situation:** Tim has two PRs fixing the exact same CI problem (the SIT Gate check kept failing on every release branch) — one on the actual release branch (`PR #75`, heading toward production), one copying that fix onto `develop` (`PR #80`, the one you asked me to review). Same fix, two places, same author.

**What happened:** while `PR #80` was going through review, CodeRabbit (the AI reviewer) found three problems with it. Tim fixed all three — but only on `PR #80`. He never carried those fixes back to `PR #75`.

**So right now, the one going to production is the worse version.** Concretely, `PR #75` is still missing:

1. **A password-like secret is shared too widely.** It sets the SIT-access secret for the whole CI job instead of just the one step that needs it — so an unrelated step (`npm install`, which runs code from every package it installs) can also see it for no reason. `PR #80` narrowed this down to just the step that needs it; `PR #75` didn't get that change.
2. **That same secret ends up in plain text in a downloadable file.** The performance-testing tool (Lighthouse) saves a report and CI uploads it as an artifact anyone with repo access can download — and that report contains the secret in readable form. `PR #80` added a step that blanks it out before uploading. `PR #75` doesn't have that step, so if it merges as-is, the secret sits there in plain text for anyone who downloads that file.
3. A smaller, lower-stakes one: it checks a narrower folder for test files than it technically should.

**Why it matters:** `PR #75` isn't some stale branch — it targets `release/v0.1.0`, which is 171 commits ahead of what's actually live and clearly the real, active release. If it merges in its current state, that secret leaks into a plaintext CI artifact on the branch that's closest to shipping.

**Why it's an easy fix:** nothing new needs to be written — it's the same three commits, already done, already reviewed, sitting right there on `PR #80`. Tim (or whoever) just needs to bring them over to `PR #75` too.

Given that — do you want me to (a) leave it to you to sort out with Tim, (b) go check what that other "PR #75 Review" session has already found before deciding, or (c) draft a comment for `PR #75` for you to look over?
